metadata.description: Fifty publicly accessible aquatic and wetland sites selected for a course-scale duck and waterfowl viewing map across Toronto and the surrounding municipalities.
metadata.coordinate_note: Coordinates are representative public viewing points or site centroids suitable for a regional Leaflet assignment, not survey-grade locations.
metadata.selection_note: Selection favours official evidence of public access plus birding, waterfowl, wetland or aquatic habitat. Evidence describes habitat suitability or documented birding value; it does not promise ducks will be present on a visit.
metadata.district_note: For Toronto, district records the six pre-amalgamation municipalities. Toronto and North York were cities immediately before amalgamation, although the six are often informally called boroughs.
metadata.responsible_viewing_note: Stay on signed paths and platforms, obey seasonal closures, keep dogs leashed where required, do not feed wildlife and do not approach nests.
metadata.geojson_use: Load with fetch(), parse as JSON, and pass the FeatureCollection to L.geoJSON().

properties.name: Grenadier Pond – High Park
properties.access: Public City park; use signed shoreline paths and viewing areas.
properties.description: A large naturalized pond and marsh remnant with established public viewpoints.
properties.evidence: City habitat and bird references support its inclusion; no abundance claim is made.

properties.name: Toronto Islands – Snug Harbour
properties.access: Public island park reached by ferry; view from public paths and shorelines.
properties.description: Sheltered harbour water and island shoreline within a large car-free public park.
properties.evidence: Official park information establishes public shoreline access and varied natural areas.

properties.name: Tommy Thompson Park
properties.access: Public pedestrian and cycling access during posted park hours; some habitat areas are restricted.
properties.description: A major lakefill nature park with wetlands, sheltered cells and open-lake shoreline.
properties.evidence: TRCA identifies the site for bird watching and significant aquatic and terrestrial habitat.

properties.name: E.T. Seton Park
properties.access: Public park and trail system; observe from signed paths and bridges.
properties.description: A broad Don Valley park with river-edge, meadow and wooded habitat.
properties.evidence: City trail information documents public Don Valley access and natural habitat.

properties.name: Taylor Creek Park
properties.access: Public ravine trail; remain on maintained paths and respect restoration areas.
properties.description: A wooded creek corridor with riparian habitat and restored wetland features.
properties.evidence: City planning documents identify creek, wetland restoration and bird habitat values.

properties.name: Humber Bay Park East
properties.access: Public waterfront paths and boardwalks; follow any construction signs.
properties.description: A shoreline peninsula with sheltered water, a pond and linear wetland.
properties.evidence: City planning identifies Humber Bay Park as important for observing overwintering waterfowl.

properties.name: Colonel Samuel Smith Park
properties.waterbody: Lake Ontario bays and marina embayment
properties.access: Public waterfront park with a network of paths.
properties.description: A lakefill park combining bays, marshes, meadows and open shoreline.
properties.evidence: City references describe the site as a birding destination and note winter waterfowl.

properties.name: Centennial Park Pond
properties.access: Public City park; use pond-side paths and obey posted restrictions.
properties.description: A large urban park pond within an extensive recreation and green-space complex.
properties.evidence: Official park planning confirms the pond and public park setting; inclusion does not assert duck abundance.

properties.name: Humber Bay Park West
properties.access: Public waterfront park with shoreline trails and lookouts.
properties.description: A peninsula offering sheltered and open-water views beside Humber Bay.
properties.evidence: The City master plan documents overwintering waterfowl use of both Humber Bay parks.

properties.name: Earl Bales Stormwater Management Pond
properties.access: Public park paths; view the pond from designated edges and trails.
properties.description: A naturalized stormwater pond connected to the West Don River system.
properties.evidence: The City documents aquatic-habitat benefits; inclusion is habitat-based, not an abundance claim.

properties.name: G. Ross Lord Park Reservoir
properties.access: Public City park with trails around the reservoir and valley.
properties.description: A large flood-control reservoir in a wooded West Don valley park.
properties.evidence: City material identifies bird and wildlife watching and potential waterfowl stopover habitat.

properties.name: Sunnybrook Park – West Don River
properties.access: Public park and ravine trails; observe from paths and bridges.
properties.description: A broad river-valley park with riparian, meadow and wooded habitat.
properties.evidence: Official trail information supports public nature access beside the Don; no direct duck-count claim is made.

properties.name: East Point Park
properties.access: Public park trails; remain outside protected meadow and shoreline areas.
properties.description: A large waterfront park containing pond, wetland and Lake Ontario habitats.
properties.evidence: The City explicitly notes the pond, wetland and extensive recorded bird diversity.

properties.name: Morningside Park – Highland Creek
properties.access: Public ravine trails and picnic areas; use bridges and maintained paths.
properties.description: A large forested ravine park centred on Highland Creek.
properties.evidence: City sources document the creek corridor, natural-area significance and wildlife habitat.

properties.name: Port Union Waterfront Park
properties.access: Public waterfront trail with shoreline overlooks.
properties.description: A restored eastern Toronto shoreline with beach, headland and aquatic-edge habitat.
properties.evidence: Official waterfront trail information establishes public shoreline access and habitat restoration.

properties.name: Smythe Park
properties.access: Public park trails; follow signed routes around ponds and creek.
properties.description: A Black Creek valley park with several ponds and wetland areas.
properties.evidence: City park-planning material explicitly identifies trails, ponds and wetlands.

properties.name: Eglinton Flats Pond
properties.waterbody: Eglinton Flats pond and Humber River
properties.access: Public City park with paths through the Humber floodplain.
properties.description: An urban pond beside the Humber River within a large floodplain park.
properties.evidence: Official City sources confirm the pond and river setting; selection is habitat-based.

properties.name: Lambton Woods
properties.access: Public ravine trail; use maintained paths and river overlooks.
properties.description: A mature Humber Valley woodland with riparian habitat and public trails.
properties.evidence: City trail information supports birding and nature viewing along the Humber corridor.

properties.name: Kariya Park
properties.access: Public City park during posted hours; view from paths and bridges.
properties.description: A compact formal garden surrounding a landscaped pond in central Mississauga.
properties.evidence: Official park information confirms pond access; inclusion preserves the original assignment site without claiming abundance.

properties.name: Rattray Marsh Conservation Area
properties.access: Public conservation trails and boardwalks; remain on marked routes.
properties.description: A protected coastal wetland and Lake Ontario shoreline with boardwalk viewing.
properties.evidence: Official conservation information documents marsh habitat, birding and public trails.

properties.name: Jim Tovey Lakeview Conservation Area
properties.access: Public conservation-area trails; winter washrooms and some nearby vehicle access are seasonal.
properties.description: A restored Lake Ontario waterfront landscape with created wetlands and shoreline habitat.
properties.evidence: Official conservation information documents wetland creation and public nature access.

properties.name: Lake Aquitaine Park
properties.access: Public City park with a loop trail around the lake.
properties.description: A large urban stormwater lake with continuous shoreline viewing opportunities.
properties.evidence: Official City information confirms the lake and public trail; no bird-abundance claim is made.

properties.name: Riverwood
properties.access: Public City park and conservation trails; stay on marked paths.
properties.description: A large natural area with Credit River, ravine, meadow and woodland habitats.
properties.evidence: City information promotes bird and nature watching in the river-valley setting.

properties.name: Meadowvale Conservation Area
properties.access: Public City conservation-area trails and river overlooks.
properties.description: A river-valley park with wetlands, forest and meadow habitat.
properties.evidence: Official sources identify bird migration viewing and a public wetland complex.

properties.name: Creditview Wetland
properties.access: Public trail and wooden viewing platform; remain on paths.
properties.description: A compact provincially significant urban wetland with a dedicated viewing platform.
properties.evidence: The City specifically identifies the platform for viewing nesting waterfowl.

properties.name: Heart Lake Conservation Park
properties.access: Seasonal TRCA park with admission and posted operating dates; use public trails and lake edges.
properties.description: A forested conservation park centred on a natural lake.
properties.evidence: TRCA lists bird watching and public nature trails; seasonal closure must be checked.

properties.name: Claireville Conservation Area
properties.access: Public TRCA trails; consult current bridge and trail-closure notices.
properties.description: A large natural area of wetlands, valleys, grasslands and river habitat.
properties.evidence: TRCA explicitly lists bird watching and describes the wetland and river system.

properties.name: Norton Place Park
properties.access: Public City park with boardwalk and paths.
properties.description: An urban lake, wetland and woodland complex with public viewing infrastructure.
properties.evidence: The City identifies the wetland and lake as critical habitat; no abundance claim is made.

properties.name: Professor's Lake
properties.access: Public lakeside park and trail; beach facilities are seasonal.
properties.description: A large urban lake with a continuous public shoreline trail.
properties.evidence: City sources document the lake and waterfowl management; selection does not imply consistent sightings.

properties.name: Loafer's Lake
properties.access: Public park paths; observe restored habitat from designated edges.
properties.description: A small lake and restored wetland connected to the Etobicoke Creek valley.
properties.evidence: The City documents wetland restoration and aquatic habitat at the lake.

properties.name: Kortright Centre for Conservation
properties.waterbody: Kortright ponds, wetlands and Humber tributaries
properties.access: TRCA site with admission and posted hours; use marked trails.
properties.description: A large conservation education property with ponds, wetlands and river habitat.
properties.evidence: TRCA runs waterbird programming focused on ducks and waders at its aquatic habitats.

properties.name: Boyd Conservation Park
properties.access: Seasonal TRCA park with admission and posted operating dates.
properties.description: A broad Humber valley park with river, forest and meadow habitat.
properties.evidence: TRCA lists Boyd as a popular bird-watching location with public trails.

properties.name: Chatfield Stormwater Management Pond
properties.access: Public sidewalk and lookout platform along the north edge; roadside parking only where permitted.
properties.description: A naturalized urban pond with a purpose-built public lookout.
properties.evidence: The City names Mallard and other water-associated birds at this birding location.

properties.name: Fletcher's Pond
properties.access: Public trail entrance near Glenkindie Avenue; park only in permitted areas.
properties.description: A neighbourhood pond with naturalized shoreline and trail access.
properties.evidence: The City birding guide specifically lists Mallard and other water-associated birds.

properties.name: North Maple Regional Park – Pondside District
properties.access: Public park paths; some Pondside areas may be affected by phased construction.
properties.description: A large regional park centred on a pond and adjacent significant wetlands.
properties.evidence: The City identifies birding, wildlife viewing and provincially significant wetland habitat.

properties.name: Milne Dam Conservation Park
properties.access: Public City park during posted hours; use trails and designated shoreline areas.
properties.description: Markham's largest municipal park, combining reservoir and Rouge River valley habitat.
properties.evidence: Official City and natural-heritage sources identify it as a major greenway and bird habitat area.

properties.name: Toogood Pond
properties.access: Public City paths and boardwalk areas around the pond.
properties.description: A central Unionville pond connected to a provincially significant marsh complex.
properties.evidence: City planning identifies Toogood Pond–Unionville Marsh as protected wetland habitat.

properties.name: Swan Lake Park
properties.access: Public City park with surrounding trails.
properties.description: A restored urban lake and park in Markham Village.
properties.evidence: The City calls Swan Lake Park highly biodiverse and an eBird hotspot for guided bird walks.

properties.name: German Mills Settlers Park
properties.access: Public valley trails; use maintained paths and bridges.
properties.description: A creek-valley park with wooded and riparian habitat.
properties.evidence: The City hosts guided migratory-bird walks at this public park.

properties.name: Rouge National Urban Park – Bob Hunter Area
properties.access: Public Parks Canada trails; a current closure affects parts of Reesor Way and Tanglewood, with signed alternatives available.
properties.description: A national urban park landscape of creek valley, restored meadow and forest.
properties.evidence: Parks Canada documents public nature access, and Markham has hosted guided migratory-bird walks in Rouge National Urban Park.

properties.name: Lake Wilcox Park
properties.access: Public waterfront promenade and boardwalk; seasonal parking fees apply and swimming is prohibited.
properties.description: A major Oak Ridges waterfront park with extensive lake-edge viewing.
properties.evidence: The City lists it among accessible birding parks and confirms public boardwalk access.

properties.name: Mill Pond Park
properties.access: Public City park with boardwalk, paths and shoreline seating.
properties.description: A large historic mill pond surrounded by an established public park.
properties.evidence: The City includes Mill Pond among its accessible birding locations.

properties.name: Newberry Park
properties.access: Public paved trail with parking; remain on the established route.
properties.description: A neighbourhood wetland park with ponds and mature trees.
properties.evidence: The City explicitly describes wetland trails, ponds and potential heron viewing.

properties.name: Phyllis Rawlinson Park – The Ponds
properties.access: Public park with parking, woodland trails and boardwalks.
properties.description: A large Oak Ridges Moraine park with boardwalks through pond habitat.
properties.evidence: City sources document The Ponds and include the park among accessible birding locations.

properties.name: Oak Ridges Corridor Conservation Reserve
properties.access: Public TRCA trail network; check seasonal parking notices and site restrictions.
properties.description: A large moraine reserve of wetlands, kettle lakes, meadows and mature forest.
properties.evidence: TRCA explicitly lists bird watching and documents wetland restoration for bird habitat.

properties.name: Petticoat Creek Conservation Park
properties.access: Seasonal TRCA park with admission and posted operating dates.
properties.description: A creek-mouth conservation park with waterfront trail and Lake Ontario views.
properties.evidence: TRCA lists bird watching and describes the creek as a wildlife corridor.

properties.name: Alex Robertson Park – Hydro Marsh
properties.access: Public City trails and viewing platforms; observe wildlife from designated areas.
properties.description: A large marsh-edge park with viewing platforms and managed nesting structures.
properties.evidence: The City documents wood-duck boxes, turtle logs, tern rafts and wetland viewing.

properties.name: Beachfront Park and Millennium Square
properties.access: Public waterfront path and elevated marsh-edge route; obey construction notices.
properties.description: A waterfront park separating Hydro Marsh from Lake Ontario.
properties.evidence: The City specifically promotes wetland bird watching from the public park.

properties.name: Altona Forest
properties.access: Public TRCA trails; no washrooms and sensitive habitat requires staying on trail.
properties.description: A significant natural area of forest, wetland and meadow habitat.
properties.evidence: TRCA explicitly lists bird watching and documents wetland and rare-species habitat.

properties.name: Rotary Frenchman's Bay West Park
properties.access: Public waterfront trail, walkways and shoreline-restoration area.
properties.description: A protected Lake Ontario bay with public western-shore viewing access.
properties.evidence: Official City information documents waterfront access and restored shoreline; inclusion is habitat-based without an abundance claim.
